title: Aether Security World - Policy / Invariant DSL AST v0.1
description: Security Policy and Invariant expression AST. Deliberately small and closed: no arbitrary code execution, no imports, no unbounded loops, no reads of the evidence view by value. Every node is a pure function of (world, action) so the oracle stays deterministic and unit-testable. Revision 1: the `evidence_view.<id>.*` ref view was REMOVED (it let a policy read an untrusted/derived evidence value straight into a condition, breaking the 'trusted_evidence_exists is the only one-way bridge' invariant); `trusted_evidence_exists` was renamed `establishing_evidence_exists` with the establishing set fixed at {trusted, semi_trusted} to match configs/default.json.

expr.$comment: Discriminated union on `op`. `ref` paths resolve against THREE views only (revision 1: was four): (1) ID view '<entity_type>.<id>.<field...>' with entity_type in {actor, resource, session, token, workflow, workflow_instance, cache, service, credential, role}; (2) ACTION-BINDING view 'action.actor.*', 'action.resource.*', 'action.session.*', 'action.token.*', 'action.workflow_instance.*', 'action.parameters.*', 'action.request.*', where the segment after 'action.' is the entity the action names - compile_spec EXPANDS these to instance paths so that decision_facts() and evidence.asserts_ref share one key space; (3) context: 'current_flow.flow_id', 'current_time'. The evidence view is reachable ONLY through the establishing_evidence_exists op, never by value. Every path resolves at compile time (Gate 2): an unresolvable path is a build error, never a silent null at oracle time. The resolver is pure - no path may mutate state.

oneOf.$comment: before(t1,t2)/after(t1,t2) compare VirtualClock timestamps; within(t1,t2,window_ms) requires 0 <= t2-t1 <= window_ms.

REVISION 1: both take exactly TWO arguments (the schema enforces two_args). state_is(workflow_instance_ref, 'PAID') checks the instance's current_state; transition_allowed(workflow_instance_ref, 'PAID') checks whether the transition from that instance's CURRENT state to the given state exists in the declared machine - the from_state is read from the binding, not passed as a third argument. Both evaluate against the declared workflow state machine, NEVER against string similarity.

lineage_depth(token_ref) = number of ancestors up the parent_token chain; lineage_root(token_ref) = the flow_id of the root ancestor. Cycles are rejected at compile time (a token cannot be its own ancestor), so these are total functions.

REVISION 1: renamed from trusted_evidence_exists and the establishing set is now explicitly {trusted, semi_trusted} = configs/default.json evidence_masking.trusted_establishes. establishing_evidence_exists(fact_key) = at least one VISIBLE evidence item asserting that canonical fact key with trust_level in the establishing set. This is the ONLY bridge from the evidence view into the decision view, and it is deliberately one-way: it can turn a verdict into insufficient_evidence, never into attack.

action.$comment: The action pattern this rule governs. `resource_type` may be omitted to mean 'any'; operation '*' matches every operation.

priority.$comment: Higher wins; ties broken by policy_id ascending (deterministic, never by evaluation order). The closed-world default-deny rule conventionally uses a negative priority so every substantive rule is evaluated first.

is_default_rule.$comment: REVISION 1: marks the closed-world fallback. world_truth=attack requires a deny from a NON-default rule or a violated invariant - a default-deny hit alone yields 'unauthorized', never 'attack' (design §8.2). Without this flag an author who forgets one allow rule could mass-produce attack labels with no security semantics.

requires_fresh.$comment: When true, a decision-critical fact established only from stale/expired evidence does NOT count as established and the oracle must return insufficient_evidence. This is the knob that makes 'stale permission cache' a first-class sample class rather than an accident.

invariant.$comment: Invariants are the only producers of world_truth. `expr` must be a total predicate over the declared world for the operations listed in applies_to; it is evaluated by the same evaluator as policies, with no side effects. REVISION 1: applies_to=['*'] means 'evaluate against whatever the action actually binds' - if the action binds no session/token/workflow_instance the invariant is recorded skipped_out_of_scope WITH a trace entry, never silently satisfied. The old wording ('must be total over every action, checked statically') was undecidable because the world's action set does not exist at compile time.

severity.$comment: REVISION 1: REPORT-ONLY triage field. It does NOT participate in the world_truth aggregation. Previously world_truth=attack required a 'critical' violation, which handed label authority to an author-writable enum: marking an invariant 'high' silently downgraded its violations to non-attacks. The aggregation rule is now category-independent: ANY violated invariant is an attack (design §8.2, ATTACK_CATEGORIES = all 20).

applies_to.$comment: Operation names this invariant governs; ['*'] means every operation. An operation not listed => skipped_out_of_scope (recorded in the trace, counted in neither satisfied nor violated). With ['*'], evaluation happens against the action's ACTUAL bindings: an unbound subject yields skipped_out_of_scope, never a silent true.

expected_violation_when.$comment: Optional human/AI-authored hypothesis about when this invariant breaks. Used ONLY as a test oracle for the invariant's own unit tests and for the diversity audit. It can never contribute a label to a dataset sample: labels come from evaluating `expr`, not from this field.
